pull_requests.title: fix(ffe): stop deterministic winner exposures while preserving holdouts
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation and Context

Opted-out subjects should retain deterministic completed winners while skipping allocations that randomize. A retained experiment link keeps winners at `doLog=true`; clearing that field based only on experiment completion also lets completed 50/50 experiments bypass opt-out.

The [author clarification](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139368#discussion_r4353896956) and [D018 producer contract](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/656696f84fb83fea87798a0d4151af0f7e2fc16d/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/backend-feedback.md#d018-randomization-is-represented-by-dolog) require the backend to represent randomization through the existing `doLog` field. This refines the [original allocation-classification RFC](https://docs.google.com/document/d/153tRlj46l-XfBGCA2X_NvxW4vwYObaH8zm2moP_AqMk/edit).

## Description

Completed standard experiments (`ROLLOUT_COMPLETE` or `CODE_REMOVED`) stop ordinary winner exposures only when delivery is deterministic. The compiler sets `doLog=true` whenever shard selection changes the variation or match/fallthrough outcome, including ordinary percentage splits and partial enrollment. This deliberately enables exposures for ordinary randomized allocations.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C["Compiled allocation"] --> R["Randomizes variation or enrollment"]
    C --> W["Deterministic completed winner"]
    C --> H["Existing active experiment or holdout logging"]
    R --> T["doLog = true"]
    H --> T
    W --> F["doLog = false; eligible for delivery"]
```

Existing active-experiment, canary, bandit, and generated-holdout logging requirements are preserved, along with the experiment link, serial IDs, and assignments. Missing lifecycle state retains logging. Lifecycle state is read in one organization-scoped snapshot query using an array parameter. The synthetic holdout runner accepts either logging value for concluded winners while retaining winner and active-experiment checks.

This PR is the Git parent of [#139379](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139379), which must inherit this change before fallback validation. [Activation metadata #139381](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139381) and [edge opt-out #140422](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/140422) have separate rollout work. Deploy the compiler and rebuild stored UFCs before enabling consumers; newly logging allocations without activation metadata retain conservative future-mode exclusion.

## How has this been tested?

After merging main at [0ae33d8f11](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/commit/0ae33d8f112685502bb8f16d8c96efbecb70219b), 918 compiler tests, 283 database repository tests, and 275 holdout-runner/primary-analysis tests pass locally. Main's golden snapshot required seven intentional `doLog` updates; all assignment data remains unchanged. The classifier matches independent raw-bucket enumeration for 500 generated cases. Restoring the old `doLog` output fails the completed 50/50, ordinary 50/50, and partial-enrollment regressions; restoring the fix passes both Go suites uncached.

[Draft contract #55](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/55) retains the source pins, negative controls, and native receipts. Seven new Lean composition theorems bring its audit to 53, with 313 existing semantic cases and 36 operational cases passing. These prove the model's composition; native classifier correctness is covered separately by the compiler tests. Handler lifecycle tests and the combined edge flow were not rerun in this update; local validation is not deployed proof.

## What is expected of reviewers?

Review the randomization classification, preservation of deterministic winner delivery and holdout exposures, and organization-scoped snapshot query. Confirm D018's exposure-logging consequence for ordinary randomized allocations and retain the separate rollout gates.

inline_comments.body:
🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron Silverman:** **[P1]** A concluded standard experiment that still splits traffic now compiles with `doLog=false`, so it randomizes opted-out subjects. Please base opt-out eligibility on randomization, not on `doLog` alone. We want a concluded experiment to behave like a randomized allocation that was never an experiment, and we want opted-out subjects to skip both, because both randomize. The exclusion in #140422 checks only `doLog`, so it skips neither. The RFC reuses `doLog` alone, so this needs a product decision. This line derives `doLog` for standard experiments from experiment state alone. That adds a new way to reach the state above: the deprecated PATCH `experiment_action: CONCLUDED` sets `ROLLOUT_COMPLETE` without rolling out the winner (`experiment_service.go:653`, called from `experiment_handler.go:2584`). The allocation keeps its split and now compiles with `doLog=false`. I put the evaluator-side change in my comment on #140422 at `experimentation.rs:62`.
Evidence — 1. a completed standard experiment that still splits compiles with doLog=false I added a `TestWinnerExposureLifecycle` row at `3e99ba2a`: a standard experiment with `completed: true` and weights 50/50. The compiled allocation has `doLog=false`, and the split stays.
Evidence — 2. callers still send the deprecated field `ffe.experimentation.experiment.patch_lifecycle_deprecated{field:experiment_action}`, summed over the 30 days to 2026-10-21: us1 95, eu1 28, us5 17, us3 13. The handler counts each request before later checks can reject it (`experiment_handler.go:2259-2264`), and the metric records neither the action nor the outcome. So these are requests that set the field, not successful concludes.
Evidence — 3. opted-out subjects are randomized A probe on the #140422 evaluators, in immediate mode, with a `doLog=false` allocation that splits 50/50 between two variations before a fallback: 200 opted-out subjects got `a` 106 and `b` 94, and none reached the fallback. The JSON and archived evaluators agree on every subject.

inline_comments.body:
🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron Silverman:** **[P2]** Update the synthetic-data holdout runner. It still requires `doLog=true` on a concluded winner. `_stage_is_ready` returns false when the ordinary allocation reports `doLog=false`, also after conclusion (`tools/synthetic_data/core/holdout_runner.py:346`). This PR compiles a concluded standard winner with `doLog=false` (`ufc.go:179`), as this test asserts. So a stage never becomes ready while its evaluations include a concluded ordinary allocation with `doLog=false`. `holdout_primary.py:138` calls the same check with every experiment concluded.
Evidence — probe test, before and after - The test below fails at `3e99ba2a`: `_stage_is_ready` returns `False` for concluded winners served with `doLog=false`. - With the fix, it passes. `tests/test_holdout_runner.py`, `tests/test_holdout_primary.py` and the probe pass: 254 tests. - The fix also accepts `doLog=true` after conclusion, so the runner works against a compiler with or without this PR.
Suggested patch — accept a non-logging winner after conclusion ```diff --- a/domains/ffe/tools/synthetic_data/core/holdout_runner.py +++ b/domains/ffe/tools/synthetic_data/core/holdout_runner.py @@ -343,7 +343,8 @@ if result["variant"] != control or result["reason"] != "DEFAULT": return False elif allocation == ordinary: - if not metadata["doLog"]: + # A concluded experiment serves its winner without exposure logging. + if key not in concluded and not metadata["doLog"]: return False if key in concluded and result["variant"] != (config["ship"] or control): return False ``` Add to `tests/test_holdout_runner.py`: ```python def _ordinary(key, variant, do_log): return { "variant": variant, "reason": "TARGETING_MATCH", "metadata": {"doLog": do_log, "allocationKey": f"{key}-allocation", "__dd_split_serial_id": 7}, } def test_concluded_ordinary_winner_without_exposure_logging_is_ready(): runner = _runner() concluded = {key: [_ordinary(key, runner.experiments[key]["ship"] or runner.experiments[key]["variants"][0]["id"], False)] for key in runner.experiments} assert RealisticHoldoutRunner._stage_is_ready(runner, concluded, set(), set(runner.experiments)) ```
